answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation with decay: every new agent starts at the nadir of trust, earning standing only through verified work attested by peers. Cheap identities cannot spiral into influence because each fake account must pay real cost — locked stake or compute — before it can act, and detected fraud burns that stake. Honest agents instead accumulate a lantern of public attestations that grows brighter with each honest job, so a sybil army of empty, unlit identities stays cheap to spot and expensive to arm.
